intro: Welcome to B2 reading! At B1 you found the main idea, told facts from opinions and skimmed short articles. Now you read longer texts like a professional: you skim and scan against the clock, read between the lines to find what the writer means but doesn't say, and find your way around long reports and opinion articles.
teachingNotes: Build on b1-reading-articles (main idea vs details, fact vs opinion, skimming about 1 minute for 120 words): recap it in one line, don't re-teach it. B2 texts are reports, news comments and opinion articles of 100–300 words on adult topics: urban flooding policy, the remote-work debate, a product launch report, a city's public transport survey. Every answer comes from the text, never from general knowledge or the learner's own opinion.

Skim vs scan: skim = the gist in 30–60 seconds for a one-page article (title, summary or first paragraph, first sentence of each paragraph, last paragraph). Scan = one fact (a name, number, date or place) in 10–20 seconds: decide what the answer looks like (capital letter, digits, %, Rp, a month), look for the key word AND its synonyms (people who use the bus = passengers), stop, then read that sentence carefully (not, only, before, target vs result, this year vs last year). The task decides: 'What is it about?' → skim; 'When? How many? Who?' → scan. Common errors: reading every word from the start; grabbing the first number they see (another number in the text, last year's figure, the target instead of the result); number formats: English 2,400 = Indonesian 2.400 and English 6.5 = Indonesian 6,5.

Inference = what the writer implies but doesn't say (makna tersirat vs tersurat, known from school). Clues: tone words (only, just, finally, still, even, yet again, surprisingly), what is emphasised (two facts placed side by side, repetition, what comes first or last), what is left out (a report with many lines about rent and few about 'trust'), and quotation marks around a word (HR calls this “normal” = the writer doubts it). An inference must be supported by specific words: always ask 'Which words show it?'. Common errors: an answer that goes too far (a prediction or a judgement the text doesn't support), an answer from the learner's own knowledge or opinion, and taking a view the writer reports as the writer's own. Indonesian learners also tend to read polite, indirect English as neutral ('The results were not what we hoped for' = bad results).

Attitude: positive (welcome, impressive, a real step forward, enthusiastic), critical (disappointing, fails to, yet again, too little too late), cautious (may, might, so far, promising but…, it is too early to say), neutral (facts and numbers only, typical of reports). The words after but / however often carry the real attitude. Cautious is not critical: a cautious writer isn't against the plan, just not sure yet. Irony is only a note for recognition: the writer says the opposite of what they mean ('Great news: the new drains are ready, just in time for the dry season' = critical), like menyindir in Indonesian. Test only clear cases; for typed attitude answers accept close synonyms (critical / negative / disappointed / sceptical).

Long reports and opinion articles: a report has a title, a summary (executive summary), background and method, findings or results, and a conclusion or recommendations. Reading order: title and summary → conclusion or last paragraph → headings to jump to the section the task needs → topic sentences → details only where needed. In an opinion article the writer's view is usually in the first and last paragraphs; the middle gives reasons and often the other side (Some people say… / Critics argue… / Of course… But…). Don't translate every word: skip words the task doesn't need or guess them from context; many learners translate sentence by sentence or paste the whole text into Google Translate, which is slow and loses the writer's point. Typed answers: accept any short phrase with the same meaning; an answer in Indonesian shows understanding but ask for English.

Limits: texts use A0–B1 grammar only (present simple passive and past simple passive, reported statements and defining relative clauses are fine). No third conditional, wish, past modals, participle clauses or non-defining relative clauses; if a learner meets one in a real text, treat it as a phrase to remember. Don't teach formal argument analysis, logical fallacies or essay structure (b2-essay-writing), and don't test irony or sarcasm beyond clear cases.

keyPoints.title: Skim and scan against the clock
keyPoints.explanation: Skim = read fast for the gist: 30–60 seconds for a one-page article (title, summary, first sentences, last paragraph). Scan = find one fact (a name, number, date or place) in 10–20 seconds: know what the answer looks like, look for the key word or a word with the same meaning, stop, then read that sentence carefully. The task decides: 'What is it about?' → skim; 'When? How many? Who?' → scan.

examples.id: Berapa orang yang menjawab survei? (scan: cari angka)

examples.id: Laporan ini terutama tentang apa? (skim: judul, ringkasan, kalimat pertama)

id.title: Skimming dan scanning dengan batas waktu
id.explanation: Skim = membaca cepat untuk menangkap inti (gist): 30–60 detik untuk artikel satu halaman (judul, ringkasan, kalimat-kalimat pertama, paragraf terakhir). Scan = mencari satu fakta (nama, angka, tanggal atau tempat) dalam 10–20 detik: bayangkan dulu bentuk jawabannya, cari kata kuncinya atau kata lain yang artinya sama, berhenti, lalu baca kalimat itu dengan teliti. Tugasnya yang menentukan: 'Tentang apa?' → skim; 'Kapan? Berapa? Siapa?' → scan.

keyPoints.title: Reading between the lines: inference and attitude
keyPoints.explanation: Inference = understanding what the writer implies but doesn't say. Clues: tone words (only, finally, yet again, even), what is emphasised (two facts side by side), what is left out, and words in quotation marks. Always point to the words that show it. Attitude = how the writer feels: positive, critical, cautious (may, so far, too early to say) or neutral. With irony, the writer says the opposite of what they mean.

examples.en: Only 40 people came to the “big” public meeting.
examples.id: Hanya 40 orang yang datang ke rapat umum yang “besar” itu. (tersirat: rapatnya sama sekali tidak besar)

examples.en: So far, the results look promising.
examples.id: Sejauh ini, hasilnya terlihat menjanjikan. (sikap: hati-hati)

examples.en: Yet again, the project is late.

id.title: Membaca yang tersirat: inferensi dan sikap penulis
id.explanation: Inferensi = memahami apa yang disiratkan penulis tetapi tidak ditulis langsung (makna tersirat). Petunjuknya: kata-kata kecil yang memberi nada (only, finally, yet again, even), apa yang ditekankan (dua fakta yang diletakkan berdampingan), apa yang tidak disebut, dan kata di dalam tanda kutip. Selalu tunjukkan kata-kata yang membuktikannya. Sikap (attitude) = perasaan penulis tentang topiknya: positif, kritis, hati-hati (may, so far, too early to say) atau netral. Dalam ironi, penulis mengatakan kebalikan dari maksudnya.

keyPoints.title: Long reports and opinion articles
keyPoints.explanation: Use the text's map: read the title and summary, then the conclusion, then use the headings and topic sentences to find the part your task needs. In an opinion article, the writer's view is usually in the first and last paragraphs; 'Some people say…' or 'Critics argue…' is someone else's view. Don't translate every word: skip the words your task doesn't need, or guess them from the words around them.

examples.id: Ringkasan → Kesimpulan → Judul bagian → Detail (urutan membaca)

examples.en: Critics argue that the plan is too expensive.
examples.id: Para pengkritik berpendapat bahwa rencana itu terlalu mahal. (pendapat orang lain, bukan penulis)

id.title: Laporan panjang dan artikel opini
id.explanation: Pakai "peta" teksnya: baca judul dan ringkasan, lalu kesimpulan, lalu pakai judul-judul bagian (headings) dan kalimat utama untuk menemukan bagian yang dibutuhkan tugasmu. Di artikel opini, pendapat penulis biasanya ada di paragraf pertama dan terakhir; 'Some people say…' (ada yang bilang…) atau 'Critics argue…' (para pengkritik berpendapat…) adalah pendapat orang lain. Jangan menerjemahkan setiap kata: lewati kata yang tidak dibutuhkan tugasmu, atau tebak artinya dari kata-kata di sekitarnya.

guidedPractice.prompt: A long article about MRT fares has one sentence with the price of a monthly pass. You need that price. Do you skim or scan? Write skim or scan.
guidedPractice.hint: You need one fact (a price), not the general idea.

guidedPractice.prompt: Scan for one number: 'The new bus line in Makassar carried 1.2 million passengers in March, up from 900,000 in February. The city wants 2 million a month by December.' How many passengers did the line carry in February?
guidedPractice.hint: Find the word February, then read the number next to it. 1.2 million is March; 2 million is the target.

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'The new banking app finally works on older phones, two years after users first asked for it.' How does the writer feel about the delay? Write pleased, critical or neutral.
guidedPractice.hint: Look at finally and two years after: does the writer think it was quick?

guidedPractice.prompt: Read: 'The early results look promising, but it is too early to say if the new bus lanes will reduce traffic.' What is the writer's attitude: positive, critical or cautious?
guidedPractice.hint: promising is positive, but what comes after but?

independentPractice.prompt: Read: 'HR calls the 40-hour weekend training “optional”. Last year, nobody who skipped it got a bonus.' Is the training really optional? Write yes or no.
independentPractice.hint: Why is optional in quotation marks? What happened to people who didn't go?

independentPractice.prompt: A report has these headings: Summary, Method, Findings, Recommendations. Under which heading do you find what the writers think the company should do next?
independentPractice.hint: Which word means suggestions for what should happen?

independentPractice.prompt: You read an opinion article. Which two paragraphs usually give the writer's own view?
expected: the first and the last paragraphs
the first and the last paragraph
the first paragraph and the last paragraph
independentPractice.hint: The beginning and the end of the article.

assessment.prompt: Scan for one date. 'NUSAPHONE 6 LAUNCH REPORT · NusaTech showed its new phone, the NusaPhone 6, at an event in Jakarta on 2 September. The phone has a bigger battery and a new camera, and it costs Rp6.5 million. It went on sale in Malaysia and Singapore on 9 September, and NusaTech says it will go on sale in Indonesia on 1 October. The company started work on the phone in March last year. More than 3,000 people came to the launch event, and 40,000 people watched it online.' When will the phone go on sale in Indonesia?
assessment.rubric: Correct: 1 October, in any date format. '9 September' = 0 (that's Malaysia and Singapore). '2 September' = 0 (the launch event). 'March' = 0 (when work started). 'October' without the day = 60. The right date in Indonesian ('1 Oktober') = 80.

assessment.prompt: Skim this report in 30 seconds. 'BANDUNG TRANSPORT SURVEY 2026 · A: In June, 5,000 people answered questions about the city's buses and trains. Most of them were students and office workers. B: Price was not the main problem: 70% said a ticket of Rp4,000 is fair. People were much more worried about how often the buses come and how long the trips take. C: Many women said they feel unsafe at bus stops at night. They asked for better lights and more security staff at the busiest stops.' Which paragraph fits the heading 'Waiting, not paying'? Write A, B or C.
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (price is fine; the problem is how often the buses come and how long the trips take). 'A' = 0 (who answered the survey). 'C' = 0 (safety at night).

assessment.prompt: Read this extract from an opinion article. 'Every rainy season, the city promises a new plan to stop the floods, and every rainy season the water comes back. This year's plan is the same as last year's: more pumps and deeper drains. It says almost nothing about the real causes: too much concrete, too few green areas, and new buildings on land that should hold water. The city has spent Rp2 trillion on pumps in five years. Yet again, families in North Jakarta are carrying their furniture upstairs.' What is the writer's attitude to the city's flood plan? Write one word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: critical, or a close synonym (negative, disappointed, frustrated, sceptical): 'the same as last year's', 'almost nothing about the real causes' and 'Yet again' all show it. 'angry' = 70 (too strong, but the right direction). 'cautious' = 20 (the writer is sure the plan won't work, not just unsure). 'positive' or 'neutral' = 0. 'kritis' (right idea, in Indonesian) = 70.

assessment.prompt: Read part of a company report. 'From July, Kirana Digital will let all staff work from home four days a week. The CEO, Bu Maya, says the change is about “trust and freedom”. The report says little more about trust or freedom. It says a lot about the office in Sudirman: the rent is Rp4 billion a year, and the company is moving to a building half the size. The new office has 60 desks for 150 staff.' The writer doesn't say it directly: what is the real reason for the change? Write it in a few words.
acceptableAnswers: to save money on the office
to save money on office rent
assessment.rubric: Correct: money / saving on rent or office costs, in any words (the report says little about 'trust and freedom' but gives many details about rent and a smaller office). 'trust and freedom' = 0: that's what the CEO says, and the writer's quotation marks and 'says little more' show doubt. 'the new office is small' or 'not enough desks' = 40 (a detail, not the reason). The right idea in Indonesian ('menghemat uang') = 70.

assessment.prompt: You have two minutes before a meeting to understand a 30-page report, 'Public Transport in Medan: 2026 Survey'. Its sections are: 1 Summary, 2 Background, 3 How we did the survey, 4 Results by area, 5 Next steps. Which section do you read first? Write its name or number.
assessment.rubric: Correct: 1, the Summary: it gives the whole report in a few lines. '5 Next steps' = 50 (a good second section to read, but it doesn't give the findings). '2', '3' or '4' = 0: background, method and detailed results come later, only if you need them.

assessment.prompt: Read the end of an opinion article. 'Some council members say free buses will get people out of their cars. Others say the city cannot pay for them. Both groups are missing the real issue. In a survey last year, only 8% of drivers said bus tickets were too expensive. Most said the buses were too slow and too rare. Free tickets will not change that. If the city has Rp300 billion a year to spend, it should spend it on more buses and bus lanes, not on free rides.' What does the writer want the city to spend the money on? Write it in a few words.
acceptableAnswers: more buses and more bus lanes
more buses and bus lanes not free rides
on more buses and bus lanes
assessment.rubric: Correct: more buses and bus lanes (one of the two = 100 too). 'free buses' or 'free rides' = 0: that's the view of some council members, and the writer says 'not on free rides'. 'cheaper tickets' = 0 (only 8% of drivers think price is a problem). The right idea in Indonesian = 70.

blocks.text:
At B1 you **skimmed** a short article in about a minute, and you learnt to tell the **main idea** from the details and **facts** from **opinions**. At B2 the texts are longer, so you need two fast speeds. The task tells you which one.
- **Skim** = read fast for the **gist** (the general idea). Target: **30–60 seconds** for a one-page article (about 300 words). Read the title, the summary or first paragraph, the first sentence of each paragraph and the last paragraph.
- **Scan** = find **one fact**: a name, a number, a date, a place. Target: **10–20 seconds**. You don't read, you search.

**Which one?** *What is it about? What is the writer's main point?* → skim. *When? How many? Who? Where?* → scan.

id.text:
Di B1 kamu sudah **skimming** artikel pendek dalam sekitar satu menit, dan belajar membedakan **ide pokok** dari detail serta **fakta** dari **opini**. Di B2 teksnya lebih panjang, jadi kamu butuh dua kecepatan membaca. Tugasnya yang memberi tahu mana yang dipakai.
- **Skim** = membaca cepat untuk menangkap **gist** (inti, gambaran umum). Target: **30–60 detik** untuk artikel satu halaman (sekitar 300 kata). Baca judul, ringkasan atau paragraf pertama, kalimat pertama setiap paragraf, dan paragraf terakhir.
- **Scan** = mencari **satu fakta**: nama, angka, tanggal, tempat. Target: **10–20 detik**. Kamu tidak membaca, kamu mencari.

**Pakai yang mana?** *What is it about?* (tentang apa?) *What is the writer's main point?* (apa pokok pikiran penulis?) → skim. *When? How many? Who? Where?* (kapan? berapa? siapa? di mana?) → scan.

blocks.text:
**How to scan:**
- **Know what the answer looks like.** A date has a month or a year (*9 September*, *2027*). A number has digits, *%* or *Rp*. A name or a place starts with a **capital letter**.
- **Choose a key word, and think of other words for it.** The question says *people who use the bus*; the text may say *passengers* or *riders*.
- **Let your eyes run down the page.** Stop only when you see it.
- **Now read that sentence carefully.** Is it this year or last year? The target or the real result? Watch for *not*, *only*, *before*, *expected*. Texts often have several numbers, and the wrong ones are the trap.

id.text:
**Cara scanning:**
- **Bayangkan bentuk jawabannya.** Tanggal punya nama bulan atau tahun (*9 September*, *2027*). Angka punya digit, *%* atau *Rp*. Nama orang atau tempat diawali **huruf kapital**.
- **Pilih kata kunci, dan pikirkan kata lain yang artinya sama.** Pertanyaannya bilang *people who use the bus* (orang yang naik bus); teksnya mungkin bilang *passengers* atau *riders* (penumpang).
- **Biarkan matamu bergerak cepat ke bawah halaman.** Berhenti hanya saat kamu melihatnya.
- **Sekarang baca kalimat itu dengan teliti.** Tahun ini atau tahun lalu? Target atau hasil sebenarnya? Perhatikan *not* (tidak), *only* (hanya), *before* (sebelum), *expected* (diharapkan). Teks sering punya beberapa angka, dan angka yang salah itulah jebakannya.

rows.en: What is the report about?
Is the writer for or against the plan?
rows.id: Penulis setuju atau tidak dengan rencana itu?
rows.note: skim: the first and last paragraphs

rows.en: When does the new bus route start?
How many people answered the survey?
Who is leading the project?
rows.note: scan: look for a name (capital letter)

blocks.text:
**English and Indonesian write numbers the other way round.** English uses a **comma** for thousands and a **point** for decimals: *2,400 people* = 2.400 orang; *Rp6.5 million* = Rp6,5 juta; *12.5%* = 12,5%. When you scan, don't read *2,400* as "dua koma empat"!
**The habit to break:** starting at the first word and reading to the end. For a scan task, that's five minutes for a twenty-second job.

id.text:
**Bahasa Inggris dan bahasa Indonesia menulis angka secara terbalik.** Bahasa Inggris memakai **koma** untuk ribuan dan **titik** untuk desimal: *2,400 people* = 2.400 orang; *Rp6.5 million* = Rp6,5 juta; *12.5%* = 12,5%. Saat scanning, jangan membaca *2,400* sebagai "dua koma empat"!
**Kebiasaan yang harus dihentikan:** mulai dari kata pertama dan membaca sampai akhir. Untuk tugas scanning, itu lima menit untuk pekerjaan dua puluh detik.

blocks.prompt: You need the date of the next council meeting from a two-page report. What do you do?
options: Read the whole report carefully from the start.
Look quickly for a month or a year, then read that sentence.
Read only the title and the first paragraph.
blocks.explain: You need one fact, so you scan: a date has a month or a year, so your eyes look for those. Reading everything is far too slow, and the title and first paragraph give the gist, not necessarily the date.

id.prompt: Kamu butuh tanggal rapat dewan berikutnya dari laporan dua halaman. Apa yang kamu lakukan?
id.explain: Kamu butuh satu fakta, jadi kamu scanning: tanggal punya nama bulan atau tahun, jadi matamu mencari itu. Membaca semuanya terlalu lambat, dan judul serta paragraf pertama memberi inti teks, belum tentu tanggalnya.

blocks.text:
Writers don't always say everything directly. **Inference** = understanding what the writer **implies** (suggests) but doesn't say. You know this from school: *makna tersurat* (what is written) and *makna tersirat* (what is meant). Four clues:
- **Tone words**: small words that add a judgement: *only*, *just*, *finally*, *still*, *even*, *yet again*, *surprisingly*. *Only 30% of the pumps work* sounds bad; *30% of the pumps work* is just a number.
- **What is emphasised**: what the writer repeats, puts first or last, or puts **side by side**. A huge budget next to small results says: the money didn't work.
- **What is left out**: a company report with one line about "trust" and ten lines about office rent makes you think about money.
- **Quotation marks** around a word can show doubt: *HR calls this “normal”* = the writer doesn't think it's normal.

id.text:
Penulis tidak selalu mengatakan semuanya secara langsung. **Inferensi** (inference) = memahami apa yang **disiratkan** penulis (imply: diisyaratkan) tetapi tidak ditulis. Kamu tahu ini dari sekolah: *makna tersurat* (yang tertulis) dan *makna tersirat* (yang dimaksud). Ada empat petunjuk:
- **Kata-kata nada**: kata kecil yang menambah penilaian: *only* (hanya), *just* (cuma), *finally* (akhirnya), *still* (masih), *even* (bahkan), *yet again* (lagi-lagi), *surprisingly* (ternyata, mengejutkan). *Only 30% of the pumps work* terdengar buruk; *30% of the pumps work* hanya sebuah angka.
- **Apa yang ditekankan**: apa yang diulang penulis, diletakkan di awal atau di akhir, atau diletakkan **berdampingan**. Anggaran besar di sebelah hasil kecil berarti: uangnya tidak berhasil.
- **Apa yang tidak disebut**: laporan perusahaan dengan satu baris tentang "kepercayaan" dan sepuluh baris tentang sewa kantor membuatmu berpikir soal uang.
- **Tanda kutip** di sekitar sebuah kata bisa menunjukkan keraguan: *HR calls this “normal”* = penulis tidak menganggapnya normal.

rows.id: Laporan itu punya sepuluh halaman tentang desain dan satu baris tentang baterai.
rows.note: left out: the battery is probably not a strong point

blocks.text:
**An inference is not a guess.** It must come from **words in the text**. Ask: *Which words show it?* If you can't point to them, it isn't the answer. Three wrong answers to avoid:
- **Too far**: *The company will close next year.* The text doesn't go that far.
- **The opposite**: the text says something different.
- **Your own knowledge or opinion**: maybe true in real life, but not in this text.
**Indonesian trap:** polite, indirect English isn't neutral. *The results were not what we hoped for* = the results were bad.

id.text:
**Inferensi bukan tebakan.** Inferensi harus berasal dari **kata-kata di dalam teks**. Tanyakan: *Kata-kata mana yang menunjukkannya?* Kalau kamu tidak bisa menunjuknya, itu bukan jawabannya. Tiga jawaban salah yang harus dihindari:
- **Terlalu jauh**: *The company will close next year* (perusahaan itu akan tutup tahun depan). Teksnya tidak sejauh itu.
- **Kebalikannya**: teks mengatakan hal yang berbeda.
- **Pengetahuan atau pendapatmu sendiri**: mungkin benar di dunia nyata, tapi tidak ada di teks ini.
**Jebakan untuk orang Indonesia:** bahasa Inggris yang sopan dan tidak langsung bukan berarti netral. *The results were not what we hoped for* (hasilnya bukan seperti yang kami harapkan) = hasilnya buruk.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'The city spent Rp500 billion on new drains in Kemang. This year, 120 homes in the area flooded, the same number as last year.' What does the writer suggest?
options: The drains have not helped yet.
The city spent too little on the drains.
The drains will work better next year.
blocks.explain: The writer puts the big cost next to **the same number as last year**: nothing has changed. 'Too little' is the opposite of what the text stresses (a lot of money), and 'next year' goes too far: the text says nothing about the future.

id.prompt: Baca: 'The city spent Rp500 billion on new drains in Kemang. This year, 120 homes in the area flooded, the same number as last year.' Apa yang disiratkan penulis?
id.explain: Penulis meletakkan biaya besar di sebelah **the same number as last year** (jumlah yang sama dengan tahun lalu): tidak ada yang berubah. 'Terlalu sedikit' kebalikan dari yang ditekankan teks (uang yang banyak), dan 'tahun depan' terlalu jauh: teksnya tidak bicara tentang masa depan.

blocks.text:
**Attitude** = how the writer feels about the topic: for it, against it, or not sure yet. Look at the judging words (adjectives like *impressive*, adverbs like *finally*) and at *may*, *might*, *could*.
- **Positive**: *welcome*, *impressive*, *a real step forward*. Very positive = **enthusiastic**.
- **Critical**: *disappointing*, *fails to*, *yet again*, *too little, too late* → the writer is against it or sees serious problems.
- **Cautious**: *may*, *might*, *so far*, *promising, but…*, *it is too early to say* → hopeful, but not sure yet.
- **Neutral**: only facts and numbers, no judging words. Typical of reports.
Writers often mix: *a promising start, but…* is **cautious**, not positive. The words after **but** or **however** often carry the real attitude.

id.text:
**Attitude** (sikap) = perasaan penulis tentang topiknya: mendukung, menentang, atau belum yakin. Lihat kata-kata yang menilai (kata sifat seperti *impressive* = mengesankan, kata keterangan seperti *finally* = akhirnya) dan kata *may*, *might*, *could* (mungkin, bisa jadi).
- **Positive** (positif): *welcome* (patut disambut baik), *impressive* (mengesankan), *a real step forward* (langkah maju yang nyata). Sangat positif = **enthusiastic** (antusias).
- **Critical** (kritis): *disappointing* (mengecewakan), *fails to* (gagal), *yet again* (lagi-lagi), *too little, too late* (terlalu sedikit, terlalu terlambat) → penulis menentang atau melihat masalah serius.
- **Cautious** (hati-hati): *may*, *might*, *so far* (sejauh ini), *promising, but…* (menjanjikan, tapi…), *it is too early to say* (masih terlalu dini untuk mengatakan) → berharap, tapi belum yakin.
- **Neutral** (netral): hanya fakta dan angka, tanpa kata penilaian. Khas laporan.
Penulis sering mencampur: *a promising start, but…* itu **cautious**, bukan positif. Kata-kata setelah **but** atau **however** (tetapi, namun) sering membawa sikap yang sebenarnya.

rows.en: This is a welcome change for commuters.
rows.id: Ini perubahan yang patut disambut baik oleh para komuter.

rows.en: The plan fails to deal with the real problem.
rows.id: Rencana itu gagal menangani masalah yang sebenarnya.

rows.en: Yet again, the project is late.
rows.note: critical: yet again = it happened before too

id.note: kritis: yet again = sebelumnya juga begitu

rows.en: It is too early to say if the new lanes will work.
rows.id: Masih terlalu dini untuk mengatakan apakah jalur baru itu akan berhasil.

rows.en: So far, the results look promising.
rows.note: cautious: so far = only until now

id.note: hati-hati: so far = baru sampai sekarang

rows.en: Bus use rose by 12% in 2025.

blocks.text:
**Irony** (just recognise it): the writer says the **opposite** of what they mean, often with *great*, *wonderful* or *of course*. *Great news: the new drains are ready, just in time for the dry season.* The drains come when the rain is over, so the attitude is **critical**. In Indonesian it's like *menyindir*. If a happy word sits next to bad facts, stop and think.
**Cautious ≠ critical:** a cautious writer isn't against the plan, just not sure yet.

id.text:
**Ironi** (cukup dikenali saja): penulis mengatakan **kebalikan** dari maksudnya, sering dengan *great*, *wonderful* (luar biasa) atau *of course* (tentu saja). *Great news: the new drains are ready, just in time for the dry season* (kabar bagus: saluran air baru sudah siap, pas sekali untuk musim kemarau). Saluran itu datang saat hujan sudah selesai, jadi sikapnya **kritis**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia ini seperti *menyindir*. Kalau kata yang gembira berdampingan dengan fakta yang buruk, berhenti dan pikirkan.
**Cautious ≠ critical:** penulis yang hati-hati tidak menentang rencananya, hanya belum yakin.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'The new bike-sharing scheme is a real step forward for Medan. In its first month, people made 30,000 trips, twice the number the city expected.' What is the writer's attitude?
blocks.explain: **a real step forward** is a positive judgement, and the writer adds a strong result (twice the number expected). There's no may, so far or but, so it isn't cautious, and nothing is criticised.

id.prompt: Baca: 'The new bike-sharing scheme is a real step forward for Medan. In its first month, people made 30,000 trips, twice the number the city expected.' Bagaimana sikap penulisnya?
id.explain: **a real step forward** (langkah maju yang nyata) adalah penilaian positif, dan penulis menambahkan hasil yang bagus (dua kali lipat dari yang diharapkan). Tidak ada may, so far atau but, jadi bukan cautious, dan tidak ada yang dikritik.

blocks.prompt: Read: 'Wonderful: after five years and Rp3 trillion, the new road is finished. It floods every time it rains.' What is the writer's attitude?
blocks.explain: This is **irony**: *Wonderful* sits next to bad facts (five years, a huge cost, and the road floods). The writer means the opposite of wonderful, so the attitude is critical.

id.prompt: Baca: 'Wonderful: after five years and Rp3 trillion, the new road is finished. It floods every time it rains.' Bagaimana sikap penulisnya?
id.explain: Ini **ironi**: *Wonderful* (luar biasa) berdampingan dengan fakta buruk (lima tahun, biaya besar, dan jalannya banjir setiap hujan). Maksud penulis kebalikan dari luar biasa, jadi sikapnya kritis.

blocks.text:
Long texts look scary, but they come with a **map**. Use it.
**A report** usually has a title, a **summary** at the top (in business: an *executive summary*), the *background* and *method* (why and how the research was done), the **findings** or **results**, and a **conclusion** or **recommendations** (what should happen next).
**An opinion article** gives the writer's view in the **first** and **last** paragraphs; the middle gives reasons, examples and often **the other side**.

Read in this order:
- The title and the **summary** (or the first paragraph).
- The **conclusion** or the last paragraph. Yes, before the middle! Now you know where the text is going.
- The **headings**: jump to the section your task needs.
- The **topic sentence** (the first sentence) of each paragraph in that section.
- Only then, the details you need.

id.text:
Teks panjang terlihat menakutkan, tapi selalu ada **peta**-nya. Pakai peta itu.
**Laporan** (report) biasanya punya judul, **ringkasan** di bagian atas (summary; di dunia bisnis: *executive summary*), *background* dan *method* (latar belakang dan metode: mengapa dan bagaimana penelitiannya dilakukan), **findings** atau **results** (temuan atau hasil), dan **conclusion** atau **recommendations** (kesimpulan atau rekomendasi: apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan selanjutnya).
**Artikel opini** memberi pendapat penulis di paragraf **pertama** dan **terakhir**; bagian tengahnya berisi alasan, contoh, dan sering juga **pendapat pihak lain**.

Baca dengan urutan ini:
- Judul dan **ringkasan** (atau paragraf pertama).
- **Kesimpulan** atau paragraf terakhir. Ya, sebelum bagian tengah! Sekarang kamu tahu ke mana arah teksnya.
- **Judul-judul bagian** (headings): langsung lompat ke bagian yang dibutuhkan tugasmu.
- **Kalimat utama** (topic sentence: kalimat pertama) setiap paragraf di bagian itu.
- Baru setelah itu, detail yang kamu perlukan.

rows.en: Summary / Executive summary
rows.note: read first: the whole report in a few lines

id.note: baca pertama: seluruh laporan dalam beberapa baris

rows.en: Background
Method
Findings / Results
Recommendations / Next steps
Critics argue that…
rows.note: someone else's view, not the writer's

rows.en: Of course, … But…
rows.note: the writer accepts a point, then gives their own view after But

id.note: penulis mengakui satu hal, lalu memberi pendapatnya sendiri setelah But

blocks.text:
**Whose view is it?** Opinion articles report other people's views: *Some managers say…*, *Critics argue…*, *Residents believe…*. That isn't the writer's view. Look for *I think*, *in my view*, *should*, and for what comes after *But* or *However*.
**Don't translate every word.** A long B2 text will have many new words. Ask: do I need this word for my task? If not, skip it. If yes, guess it from the words around it, then check. Translating a two-page report sentence by sentence (or pasting it all into Google Translate) takes an hour, and you can still miss the writer's point.

id.text:
**Ini pendapat siapa?** Artikel opini melaporkan pendapat orang lain: *Some managers say…* (sebagian manajer bilang…), *Critics argue…* (para pengkritik berpendapat…), *Residents believe…* (warga percaya…). Itu bukan pendapat penulis. Cari *I think*, *in my view* (menurut saya), *should* (sebaiknya), dan apa yang muncul setelah *But* atau *However*.
**Jangan menerjemahkan setiap kata.** Teks B2 yang panjang pasti punya banyak kata baru. Tanyakan: apakah aku butuh kata ini untuk tugasku? Kalau tidak, lewati. Kalau ya, tebak artinya dari kata-kata di sekitarnya, lalu cek. Menerjemahkan laporan dua halaman kalimat demi kalimat (atau menempelkan semuanya ke Google Translate) makan waktu satu jam, dan kamu tetap bisa melewatkan maksud penulis.

blocks.prompt: In an opinion article you read: 'Critics argue that the new bus lanes make traffic worse.' Whose view is this?
options: Other people's view, reported by the writer
blocks.explain: **Critics argue that…** tells you what other people think. The writer may agree or disagree: look for the writer's own words (in my view, should, But…) later in the article. There's no number or source, so it isn't a survey fact.

id.prompt: Di sebuah artikel opini kamu membaca: 'Critics argue that the new bus lanes make traffic worse.' Ini pendapat siapa?
id.explain: **Critics argue that…** memberi tahu apa yang dipikirkan orang lain. Penulis bisa setuju atau tidak: cari kata-kata penulis sendiri (in my view, should, But…) di bagian selanjutnya. Tidak ada angka atau sumber, jadi ini bukan fakta dari survei.

material.title: Putting it together: one opinion article

blocks.text:
Skim first (45 seconds): the title, the first paragraph and the last paragraph. Then answer the three questions below. (*groundwater* = water under the ground; *piped water* = water from the city's pipes; *sinking* = slowly going down.)

**A WALL WILL NOT SAVE NORTH JAKARTA**
Last month the government showed its new plan for North Jakarta: a 12-kilometre sea wall, 50 new pumps and a budget of Rp40 trillion. Officials say the wall will protect two million people. It is an impressive number.

But walls only stop water from the sea. In February, the worst floods came from the rivers and the rain, not from the sea. And the city is still sinking: in some areas the ground goes down about 10 centimetres a year, mostly because homes, hotels and factories pump water from under the ground.

The plan has 40 pages about the wall. It has one page about groundwater.

Of course, the city needs to protect its coast. But in my view, the money should go first to clean piped water for every home, so that people and companies can stop pumping water from under the ground. A wall is easy to see. Land that stops sinking is harder to see, but it matters more.

id.text:
Skim dulu (45 detik): judul, paragraf pertama, dan paragraf terakhir. Lalu jawab tiga pertanyaan di bawah. (*groundwater* = air tanah; *piped water* = air ledeng/PAM; *sinking* = ambles, turun.)

**A WALL WILL NOT SAVE NORTH JAKARTA**
Last month the government showed its new plan for North Jakarta: a 12-kilometre sea wall, 50 new pumps and a budget of Rp40 trillion. Officials say the wall will protect two million people. It is an impressive number.

But walls only stop water from the sea. In February, the worst floods came from the rivers and the rain, not from the sea. And the city is still sinking: in some areas the ground goes down about 10 centimetres a year, mostly because homes, hotels and factories pump water from under the ground.

The plan has 40 pages about the wall. It has one page about groundwater.

Of course, the city needs to protect its coast. But in my view, the money should go first to clean piped water for every home, so that people and companies can stop pumping water from under the ground. A wall is easy to see. Land that stops sinking is harder to see, but it matters more.

blocks.prompt: Scan: how fast is the ground going down in some areas?
blocks.explain: Scan for a number next to **ground** and **a year**: about 10 centimetres. 12 is the length of the wall in kilometres and 50 is the number of pumps: other numbers are the trap.

id.prompt: Scan: seberapa cepat tanahnya turun di beberapa daerah?
id.explain: Cari angka di dekat kata **ground** (tanah) dan **a year** (per tahun): sekitar 10 sentimeter. 12 adalah panjang tembok dalam kilometer dan 50 adalah jumlah pompa: angka-angka lain itulah jebakannya.

blocks.prompt: 'The plan has 40 pages about the wall. It has one page about groundwater.' What does the writer suggest?
options: The plan doesn't take groundwater seriously enough.
Groundwater isn't a problem in North Jakarta.
blocks.explain: The writer puts 40 pages next to one page, in a paragraph of its own: that emphasis says groundwater gets too little attention. The length of the plan isn't the point, and the writer clearly thinks groundwater is a big problem (the city is sinking because of it).

id.prompt: 'The plan has 40 pages about the wall. It has one page about groundwater.' Apa yang disiratkan penulis?
id.explain: Penulis meletakkan 40 halaman di sebelah satu halaman, dalam paragraf tersendiri: penekanan itu berarti masalah air tanah kurang diperhatikan. Panjang rencananya bukan intinya, dan penulis jelas menganggap air tanah masalah besar (kota ini ambles karenanya).

blocks.prompt: What does the writer think the money should go to first?
options: Clean piped water for every home
blocks.explain: The last paragraph has the writer's view: **in my view, the money should go first to clean piped water**. The wall and the pumps are the government's plan; the writer reports them and then says **But**.

id.prompt: Menurut penulis, uangnya sebaiknya dipakai pertama-tama untuk apa?
id.explain: Paragraf terakhir berisi pendapat penulis: **in my view, the money should go first to clean piped water** (menurut saya, uangnya sebaiknya dipakai dulu untuk air ledeng yang bersih). Tembok dan pompa adalah rencana pemerintah; penulis melaporkannya lalu berkata **But**.

id.intro: Selamat datang di membaca level B2! Di B1 kamu sudah menemukan ide pokok, membedakan fakta dan opini, dan skimming artikel pendek. Sekarang kamu membaca teks yang lebih panjang seperti seorang profesional: skimming dan scanning dengan batas waktu, membaca yang tersirat (maksud penulis yang tidak ditulis langsung), dan menjelajahi laporan panjang serta artikel opini dengan cepat.

assessment.rs-1: Scan untuk satu tanggal. 'NUSAPHONE 6 LAUNCH REPORT · NusaTech showed its new phone, the NusaPhone 6, at an event in Jakarta on 2 September. The phone has a bigger battery and a new camera, and it costs Rp6.5 million. It went on sale in Malaysia and Singapore on 9 September, and NusaTech says it will go on sale in Indonesia on 1 October. The company started work on the phone in March last year. More than 3,000 people came to the launch event, and 40,000 people watched it online.' Kapan ponsel ini mulai dijual di Indonesia? Tulis tanggalnya dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.rs-2: Skim laporan ini dalam 30 detik. 'BANDUNG TRANSPORT SURVEY 2026 · A: In June, 5,000 people answered questions about the city's buses and trains. Most of them were students and office workers. B: Price was not the main problem: 70% said a ticket of Rp4,000 is fair. People were much more worried about how often the buses come and how long the trips take. C: Many women said they feel unsafe at bus stops at night. They asked for better lights and more security staff at the busiest stops.' Paragraf mana yang cocok dengan judul 'Waiting, not paying' (menunggu, bukan membayar)? Tulis A, B atau C.
assessment.rs-3: Baca kutipan artikel opini ini. 'Every rainy season, the city promises a new plan to stop the floods, and every rainy season the water comes back. This year's plan is the same as last year's: more pumps and deeper drains. It says almost nothing about the real causes: too much concrete, too few green areas, and new buildings on land that should hold water. The city has spent Rp2 trillion on pumps in five years. Yet again, families in North Jakarta are carrying their furniture upstairs.' Bagaimana sikap penulis terhadap rencana banjir kota itu? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.rs-4: Baca bagian laporan perusahaan ini. 'From July, Kirana Digital will let all staff work from home four days a week. The CEO, Bu Maya, says the change is about “trust and freedom”. The report says little more about trust or freedom. It says a lot about the office in Sudirman: the rent is Rp4 billion a year, and the company is moving to a building half the size. The new office has 60 desks for 150 staff.' Penulis tidak mengatakannya langsung: apa alasan sebenarnya dari perubahan ini? Tulis dalam beberapa kata bahasa Inggris.
assessment.rs-5: Kamu punya dua menit sebelum rapat untuk memahami laporan 30 halaman, 'Public Transport in Medan: 2026 Survey'. Bagian-bagiannya: 1 Summary, 2 Background, 3 How we did the survey, 4 Results by area, 5 Next steps. Bagian mana yang kamu baca pertama? Tulis nama atau nomornya.
assessment.rs-6: Baca bagian akhir sebuah artikel opini. 'Some council members say free buses will get people out of their cars. Others say the city cannot pay for them. Both groups are missing the real issue. In a survey last year, only 8% of drivers said bus tickets were too expensive. Most said the buses were too slow and too rare. Free tickets will not change that. If the city has Rp300 billion a year to spend, it should spend it on more buses and bus lanes, not on free rides.' Menurut penulis, uangnya sebaiknya dipakai untuk apa? Tulis dalam beberapa kata bahasa Inggris.
